events.title: The Senate grants Augustus the title pater patriae
events.description: The Roman Senate gave Augustus the title pater patriae, 'father of the country', which was then inscribed in Rome, including in the Senate chambers in the Forum Romanum. Under the Republic it had been awarded only to Camillus and Cicero.

events.title: Earthquake strikes Pompeii and Herculaneum
events.description: A strong earthquake badly damaged towns around the Bay of Naples. Pompeii was still being repaired seventeen years later when Vesuvius buried it in 79.
events.html: A strong earthquake badly damaged towns around the Bay of Naples. Pompeii was still being repaired seventeen years later when Vesuvius buried it in 79.

events.title: An Lushan proclaims himself emperor of Yan at Luoyang
events.description: The rebel Tang general An Lushan declared himself emperor at Luoyang on the Lunar New Year, founding the state of Yan, and named Zhang Tongru and the surrendered Tang official Daxi Xun his chancellors. Yan collapsed in 763.
events.html: The rebel Tang general An Lushan declared himself emperor at Luoyang on the Lunar New Year, founding the state of Yan, and named Zhang Tongru and the surrendered Tang official Daxi Xun his chancellors. Yan collapsed in 763.

events.title: Twenty-six Christians crucified at Nagasaki
events.description: On the orders of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, six Franciscan missionaries, Japanese Jesuits and lay converts were crucified on a hill at Nagasaki. They are honoured as the Twenty-Six Martyrs of Japan.
events.html: On the orders of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, six Franciscan missionaries, Japanese Jesuits and lay converts were crucified on a hill at Nagasaki. They are honoured as the Twenty-Six Martyrs of Japan.

events.title: Calabrian earthquakes begin in southern Italy
events.description: The first of five major shocks struck Calabria and Sicily, beginning a sequence that lasted weeks. Around 30,000 to 50,000 people died, and the disaster prompted early scientific study of earthquakes.
events.html: The first of five major shocks struck Calabria and Sicily, beginning a sequence that lasted weeks. Around 30,000 to 50,000 people died, and the disaster prompted early scientific study of earthquakes.

events.title: New Hermitage museum opens to the public in St Petersburg
events.description: Nicholas I opened the purpose-built New Hermitage to display the imperial art collections. The Hermitage is now one of the largest museums in the world.
events.html: Nicholas I opened the purpose-built New Hermitage to display the imperial art collections. The Hermitage is now one of the largest museums in the world.

events.title: Britain and the United States sign the first Hay-Pauncefote Treaty
events.description: The agreement gave the United States the right to build a canal across Central America. Rejected by the Senate, it was renegotiated in 1901, opening the way for the Panama Canal.
events.html: The agreement gave the United States the right to build a canal across Central America. Rejected by the Senate, it was renegotiated in 1901, opening the way for the Panama Canal.

events.title: BBC broadcasts the Greenwich time signal for the first time
events.description: The six short 'pips', generated by the Royal Observatory at Greenwich, were broadcast to mark the hour. The signal is still heard on BBC radio today.
events.html: The six short 'pips', generated by the Royal Observatory at Greenwich, were broadcast to mark the hour. The signal is still heard on BBC radio today.

events.title: Apollo 14 lands at Fra Mauro
events.description: Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell landed in the lunar highlands, the target of the aborted Apollo 13. Shepard, America's first astronaut in space, became the fifth person to walk on the Moon.
